manufacturer.trigem.description: South Korean computer manufacturer also known as Sambo Computer and TG Sambo, active under its own brands and as an international OEM.
manufacturer.trigem.history:
TriGem began in Seoul in 1980, when the personal computer was not yet an everyday product in South Korea. The company—also known at different times as Sambo Computer or TG Sambo—identifies the 1981 SE-8001 as the country’s first PC. Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy describes it as the first personal computer commercialised domestically. More than a chronological first, the machine marks the start of a local industry able to make and sell a microcomputer in Korea.

The next stage combined its own brand with export. The TriGem 20 addressed the domestic market, while the Ministry’s public record recalls a 1982 contract for 1,200 units for Canada as Korea’s first PC export. The point is not to portray TriGem as the country’s sole manufacturer, but to show how a young company began to compete in an international chain of components, assembly and distribution.

That dual role also explains the company’s products. TriGem sold computers under its own name, but also made motherboards and systems for other companies. The SX386M board preserved by BluMach illustrates the latter: it is documented in OEM systems such as the Emerson Elite and the CMS Enhancements ESP, and must not be confused with an Olivetti or a simple rebrand. Its 80386SX processor, Headland chipset and ISA slots show an early-1990s standard PC platform adapted for different integrators.

Later corporate continuity involved new names and activities. TG&Co., established in 2011, retains the 1980 origin in its own chronology and now combines PCs, industrial devices, displays and ODM manufacture for retail brands. TriGem’s story therefore does not end with the desktop PC: it links one of Korea’s early microcomputer initiatives to the supply of devices for different markets and brands.
